<reason>PRO kept a live net-benefit path: practice-based trust where calling for help does not trigger screening travels neighbor-to-neighbor, predators lose easy prey, and witnesses solve violent crime. CON's two strongest pushes - fear is asymmetric and detainer refusal is practical release because criminal warrants are unavailable for civil status - were answered by firewall-necessity and ICE-retains-arrest/notification/judicial-warrant options, plus the point the person was already released by a judge. CON never answered liability for extra civil detention or resource diversion, dropped the two-tier claim, and its victim-versus-inmate population split was rebutted by spillover learning that any police-to-ICE pipeline chills calls.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 A1/A2 plus trade framing was decisive: reframing the file as already released by criminal law, refusing extra time as rights protection not predator release, and weighing one extra-day hold against a standing rule that removes dozens of future victims by preserving witnesses.</best_rebuttal>
